title: Greeting: an apostle not from men
summary: Paul, an apostle sent not by men but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, greets the churches of Galatia: Christ gave himself to deliver us from the present evil age.

title: No other gospel
summary: Paul is astonished the Galatians are deserting to a different gospel and says anyone, even an angel from heaven, who preaches a contrary gospel should be accursed.

title: A gospel received by revelation
summary: Paul's gospel is not man's gospel: he did not receive it from any man but through a revelation of Jesus Christ.

title: Paul's former life in Judaism
summary: Paul violently persecuted the church of God and advanced in Judaism, extremely zealous for the traditions of his fathers.

title: Called by grace; off to Arabia and Damascus
summary: God, who set Paul apart before he was born, revealed his Son to him to preach among the Gentiles; Paul consulted no one but went away into Arabia and returned to Damascus.

title: First Jerusalem visit: fifteen days with Cephas
summary: After three years Paul went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas for fifteen days, seeing no other apostle except James the Lord's brother.

title: In Syria and Cilicia; the Judean churches glorify God
summary: Paul went to Syria and Cilicia, still unknown in person to the churches of Judea, who heard that their former persecutor now preached the faith and glorified God.

title: Second Jerusalem visit with Barnabas and Titus
summary: After fourteen years Paul went up with Barnabas and Titus, set his gospel before the leaders privately, and refused to yield to false brothers; Titus, a Greek, was not forced to be circumcised.

title: The pillars give the right hand of fellowship
summary: James, Cephas and John, the 'pillars', recognized that Paul was entrusted with the gospel to the uncircumcised and gave him and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, asking only that they remember the poor.

title: Paul opposes Cephas at Antioch
summary: When Cephas withdrew from eating with Gentiles for fear of the circumcision party, and even Barnabas was led astray, Paul opposed him to his face before them all.

title: Justified by faith, not by works of the law
summary: Even Jews by birth know that a person is not justified by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ.

title: Crucified with Christ
summary: Through the law Paul died to the law; he has been crucified with Christ and now lives by faith in the Son of God, for if righteousness came through the law, Christ died for no purpose.

title: O foolish Galatians: the Spirit by hearing with faith
summary: Paul asks whether they received the Spirit by works of the law or by hearing with faith, and whether, having begun by the Spirit, they are now being perfected by the flesh.

title: Abraham believed God
summary: Abraham believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness, so those of faith are sons of Abraham, and in him all the nations are blessed.

title: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law
summary: All who rely on works of the law are under a curse, but Christ became a curse for us ('hanged on a tree') so the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles.

title: The covenant and Abraham's offspring
summary: Like a ratified human covenant, God's promise to Abraham and his offspring (singular, Christ) cannot be annulled by the law that came 430 years later.

title: Why then the law?
summary: The law was added because of transgressions until the offspring should come, put in place through angels by an intermediary, and the Scripture imprisoned everything under sin.

title: The law was our guardian
summary: Before faith came we were held captive under the law as under a guardian until Christ came; now that faith has come we are no longer under a guardian.

title: All one in Christ Jesus
summary: All who were baptized into Christ have put on Christ: there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male and female, and all are Abraham's offspring and heirs.

title: The heir who is still a child
summary: An underage heir is no different from a slave, but in the fullness of time God sent his Son so we might receive adoption as sons and cry 'Abba! Father!'

title: Turning back to weak elementary principles
summary: Having come to know God, how can the Galatians turn back to the weak and worthless elementary principles, observing days, months, seasons and years?

title: Paul's illness and the Galatians' first welcome
summary: Paul first preached to them because of a bodily ailment, and they received him as an angel of God and would have given him their eyes; has he now become their enemy by telling the truth?

title: Until Christ is formed in you
summary: The agitators court the Galatians for no good purpose, while Paul is again in the anguish of childbirth until Christ is formed in his little children.

title: Hagar and Sarah: two covenants
summary: Abraham's two sons, by a slave woman and a free woman, picture two covenants: Hagar is Mount Sinai and the present Jerusalem in slavery, but the Jerusalem above is free and is our mother.

title: Children of the free woman
summary: Like Isaac, believers are children of promise; Scripture says to cast out the slave woman and her son, for we are children of the free woman.

title: Stand firm in freedom
summary: Christ has set us free, so do not submit again to a yoke of slavery: accepting circumcision obligates one to the whole law, but in Christ only faith working through love counts.

title: A little leaven
summary: The Galatians were running well until someone hindered them; a little leaven leavens the whole lump, and Paul wishes those who unsettle them would emasculate themselves.

title: Called to freedom: serve one another
summary: Do not use freedom as an opportunity for the flesh but through love serve one another, for the whole law is fulfilled in 'love your neighbor as yourself.'

title: Walk by the Spirit
summary: Walk by the Spirit and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh, for the flesh and the Spirit are opposed to each other.

title: The works of the flesh
summary: The works of the flesh, from sexual immorality and idolatry to envy and drunkenness, are evident, and those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.

title: The fruit of the Spirit
summary: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control; those who belong to Christ keep in step with the Spirit.

title: Bear one another's burdens
summary: Restore a brother caught in transgression in a spirit of gentleness, bear one another's burdens to fulfill the law of Christ, and let each test his own work.

title: Sowing and reaping
summary: God is not mocked: whatever one sows he will reap, so let us not grow weary of doing good, especially to the household of faith.

title: Large letters: boast only in the cross
summary: Writing in large letters with his own hand, Paul says the circumcision party wants to boast in their flesh, but he boasts only in the cross, for what counts is a new creation.

title: Final greeting: the marks of Jesus
summary: Paul bears on his body the marks of Jesus and closes: the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers.
